findings.issue: The app ships with zero tests despite ~500 LOC of script logic heavy in filtering, pagination, sorting, dedup and URL-state rules.
findings.suggestion: Add a lightweight runner (node:test + Hono's app.request()) and unit-test the pure helpers in api.js (humanize, latestEnglishFlavor, toSpeciesList, mapLimit) plus route-level behaviour for '/', '/pokemon/:name', and the moves-table sort endpoint.

findings.issue: Filter/pagination logic (search substring match, combined filters, page parse/clamp, slice math, page-count text) is entirely unguarded.
findings.suggestion: Behavioural route tests: GET '/?q=pika&type=fire&page=2' asserting rendered card names, 'Page n of m' text and that 'Previous page'/'Next page' appear/disappear at the boundaries.

findings.issue: Moves assembly and sorting (default game = highest order, method ordering fallback, method:level dedup, nulls-last in both sort directions) is untested and subtle.
findings.suggestion: Test GET '/pokemon/pikachu/moves-table?...&sort=power&dir=desc' with fixture data containing null power/accuracy, asserting order and aria-sort values; test that an unknown learn method sorts alphabetically after the four known ones.

findings.issue: 'Non-hidden wins' ability resolution (existing.hidden && entry.is_hidden) is order-dependent and easy to regress into last-write-wins.
findings.suggestion: Test GET '/abilities/:name' against a fixture where a species has both a hidden and a normal entry, asserting 'Hidden ability' text presence/absence.

findings.issue: onError returns the 'Not found' page with status 500, conflating API failures with not-found; no test would catch this or any other error-path behaviour.
findings.suggestion: Test that a genuine API failure (mocked 500) and a missing resource ('/pokemon/missingno') produce distinguishable responses; consider a distinct error page.

findings.issue: movePage dereferences move.damage_class.name unguarded; a move without a damage class would throw and surface as the misleading 500 'Not found' page, and nothing tests it.
findings.suggestion: Add a null guard (render '—') and a test for a move fixture with null damage_class.

findings.issue: The only client-side code — stripping empty htmx form params so pushed URLs omit default filters — is a five-line pure-ish behaviour with no coverage.
findings.suggestion: Test it by dispatching an htmx:configRequest event (or extract the strip function and unit-test it) asserting 'q', 'type', 'generation' empties are removed.

findings.issue: Inline re-implementation of the englishGenus helper that already exists at app/src/api.js:42-43 — drift hazard, and untested either way.
findings.suggestion: Import englishGenus from api.js; add it to the humanize/englishName unit tests.

findings.issue: The process-wide index build (alternate-form exclusion via byId, slot-ordered types, generation assignment) underpins every list page and has no tests.
findings.suggestion: Unit-test buildIndex against small in-memory fixtures (inject a fake apiFetch) covering a species appearing in two types and in a generation.

summary: The app contains no tests of its own — no files, no runner, no test script — despite roughly 500 lines of exactly the risky logic (filtering, pagination, moves-table sorting and dedup, URL state, error paths) this dimension cares about. The code is unusually test-friendly: pure helpers in api.js and Hono's app.request() make behavioural tests cheap. Until someone adds them, the acceptance suite is the only guard, and any data-layer refactor will ship blind.
